decisions.reason: SOL keeps the relief and the two Supreme Peak masters while tightening the phrasing.
“Lucky or screwed” keeps the narrator’s uncertainty in a more conversational voice.
SOL preserves the near miss and his recovery without changing the action.
“Code” and “noble custom” retain the martial-world complaint and its mock-formal tone.
SOL keeps the absurdity and the lowered fist; the source does not require “slowly.”
SOL consistently carries the same “code” wording from the preceding line.
“I dropped my voice” is a natural rendering of lowering his voice; the reply follows immediately.
“Indeed” keeps the affirmative in the deliberately formal exchange.
SOL preserves the request to face them one at a time and have one stay out, in more direct spoken English.
SOL drops the “Bastard?” callback, losing the joke that he pretends not to remember insulting the old man.
SOL keeps the contrast between casual and formal speech and the old man’s frustration.
“A junior from a much later generation” naturally conveys the distant-generation junior and the apology.
The Korean describes his posture as straight as a sword; no “form” is mentioned, and SOL preserves the salute.
SOL keeps the old man’s incredulous identification as a question.
The Korean objects to hearing him talk about juniors; SOL changes this to hearing him call the old man Senior.
SOL drops the condition that everyone in the martial world is one family, changing the scope of the claim.
SOL preserves the question about his Murim Alliance position without changing its meaning.
“Out of focus” weakens the Korean’s emphatic image of eyes gone completely off the rails.
The master-and-composure thought is retained in H020, so deleting this duplicate paragraph does not drop the meaning.
SOL preserves the composure thought and the unchanged expression while combining them smoothly.
The Korean says the situation is driving him insane; SOL instead blames the other speaker.
“Every word is true” preserves the oath’s assertion that none of his claims are false.
SOL removes the pointed “little” from the old man’s trailing rebuke.
“Polite face” changes the Korean’s focus from his polite demeanor to his appearance.
“Every stitch” keeps the painstaking-effort joke, and “never met” is natural for the source’s “never seen.”
“Fuck you” replaces the direct “you bastard” insult, changing the force and target of the line.
SOL keeps the point that a lie must be believable to fool anyone.
SOL preserves the embarrassment and the demand to shut up in natural dialogue.
SOL drops the ellipsis that marks the old man’s pause before commenting on the sudden rudeness.
SOL keeps the senility taunt and the demand to be called Senior without changing the insult’s substance.
“Chuckled” matches the old man’s Korean snicker and retains the pause amid the insults.
The clipped praise preserves the joke that Jin is worthy of the Fire King’s Disciple title.
The Korean stresses that none have ever even seen the Fire King’s face; SOL drops “even.”
SOL preserves the pause and short laugh without needing to repeat the old man’s identity.
SOL retains the barely-over-twenty taunt and the challenge to speak about those days.
SOL naturally preserves his claim that he can infer what happened without having lived through it.
The following dialogue makes clear he continues speaking; the separate transition is unnecessary.
SOL keeps the threat and the idea that the old man survived by avoiding the Fire King.
“I think your luck runs out today” preserves the prediction and its hedge.
SOL keeps the correction from one target to both and the heat shimmering above the spearhead.
SOL preserves the clenched fist, forward step, and vanishing smile.
“Lunatic” preserves the accusation that only someone deranged would kill people that way.
SOL preserves that the captives are safe for now and will be killed when the Demon Empress returns.
SOL retains both the relief and the fact that the enemy confirmed two things.
SOL omits the source’s explicit “fucking bitch” insult for the Southern Heaven Demon Empress.
SOL preserves his realization and the hardening expression; the subject remains clear from context.
SOL removes the explicit Demon Empress title from the conditional statement, which the Korean names.
SOL keeps the taunt about bringing his hyung because they feared a younger opponent.
SOL retains the anger, the step forward, and its tactical significance.
SOL preserves that he had to halt the full-force spear swing in the next instant.
“As thin as a branch” preserves the withered hand’s image and the shoulder grab.
SOL drops the source’s “three-inch tongue” image, an important jab about the opponent’s words.
SOL keeps the comparison with Baeksang and the distinction in depth between the two men.
The glacier-cold composure image is retained in H055, so its deletion does not lose content.
SOL combines the glacier image and martial power into a complete, natural sentence.
“I can’t see an opening” keeps the narrator’s instinct that there is no visible gap.
The instinct’s meaning is stated in H058, so deleting this setup does not drop the conclusion.
SOL preserves the judgment that the old man is at least his equal, perhaps stronger.
SOL keeps the narrator’s attention on the silent old man while avoiding the awkward “nerves had been focused.”
The Korean says the opponent’s attention was similarly focused; SOL narrows this to watching him closely.
“Impressive” preserves the old man’s emphatic praise and self-correction.
SOL conveys the old man’s difficult-to-read admiration as he steps forward.
SOL keeps the tactic, the Demon Empress’s warning, and the forecast that Jin will become an obstacle.
SOL preserves Jin’s suspicion that the compliment carries a threat to kill him.
SOL explicitly confirms that Jin understood both the compliment and the intent to kill.
SOL retains the request to be let through and the stone-in-the-road metaphor.
SOL preserves the image of removing a stone to smooth the road ahead.
The Korean asks whether they have the skill to do it; SOL narrows that to whether they are strong enough.
SOL keeps the first old man’s angry reaction and the second man’s calm reply.
The contraction preserves the restrained answer without changing its meaning.
SOL drops the source’s emphasis that this would be an extremely difficult fight.
The mad-dog comparison is retained in H073, so this deletion does not lose the image.
SOL preserves the mad-dog contrast and the danger of a composed opponent who does not underestimate him.
The Korean specifies martial prowess; SOL recasts it as general strength.
SOL retains the even odds in a life-and-death duel and the expectation that it will not be one-on-one.
SOL keeps the cat’s-paw image and the assessment that the disheveled old man exceeds Baeksang.
SOL removes the repeated “Can I?” and loses the source’s emphatic beat of self-doubt.
SOL preserves the instinctive doubt crossing his mind just before the growl.
Muyaho’s growl and bared fangs are retained in H080, so this deletion does not drop the action.
SOL retains Muyaho’s warning growl, crouch, readiness to spring, and refusal to retreat.
SOL preserves the narrator’s profane resolve not to back down because Muyaho will fight.
The one troubling point is stated in H083, so this deletion does not lose the thought.
SOL retains his worry that he might not be able to protect Muyaho.
The uncertainty is carried into H085’s “I couldn’t tell whether,” so the separate line is redundant.
SOL preserves both possibilities: the tiger read his eyes or understood his wish that it flee.
SOL keeps the transition to the certainty that follows.
SOL shifts the source’s future-oriented either-or declaration into past tense; BASE preserves the resolve.
The refusal to retreat is retained in H087, so this deletion does not omit it.
SOL preserves the crude instruction to peel and eat their limp dicks before stating their sobriquets.
SOL preserves White Flame lowered at his side and the old man’s killing-intent smile.
SOL keeps the mocking dismissal of Black Hand as an unknown nobody.
SOL preserves the old man’s explanation for being unknown and his promised notoriety as Jin’s killer.
SOL keeps the boast that everyone who dies by Jin’s hand becomes famous.
SOL preserves his calm answer, dismissal of Black Hand’s reaction, and turn toward the other old man.
SOL omits that the other old man’s response was contrary to Jin’s wishes.
SOL retains the point that a known sobriquet makes an enemy easy to assess.
SOL preserves the knowledge imbalance and challenge without mechanically repeating “this old man.”
SOL keeps the die-cast metaphor and the need to see how it lands.
“Curled in my lower dantian” preserves the fire dragon’s position and awakening.
SOL changes the erupted aura to a wave of qi, losing the source’s established aura term and image.
“Burned away poison” preserves the heat’s effect while reading naturally.
SOL retains the Black Hand Fist Demon’s sharpening focus and the strange light in the other man’s eyes.
SOL keeps the weapon emerging from the sleeve and its blue gleam; the next paragraph carries the attack.
“Twin wheels” identifies the paired weapon; SOL’s “two wheels” loses that category.
SOL retains the reduced numbers and the need to move faster, consolidating the following sentence.
The need to move faster is already preserved in H105, so this deletion loses no meaning.
“Doing so now” clearly refers to turning back and preserves the consequence for his sacrifice.
SOL keeps the self-correction from him to Jin Taekyung and the unobstructed path.
SOL preserves the race north ahead of the messenger pigeon and the warriors’ pursuit of Jin.
The Korean says they climbed over mountains; SOL changes that physical action to crossing them.
The source describes a tense, urgent journey; “desperate” changes that characterization.
The Korean describes Namho’s shout directed below the hill; SOL changes the action to pointing.
“Followed one another” naturally conveys the warriors advancing in a trailing line.
SOL preserves their arrival at the reconnaissance squad, relief, and thought of one person.
SOL states what he was doing as definite; the Korean preserves uncertainty about what he might be doing.
